issues: The limitations section incorrectly states that only two admitted sources are abstract-only. Three supplied analyses are marked access="abstract_only": doi-10-1007-978-3-319-67684-5-24, doi-10-1016-j-eswa-2021-115626, and doi-10-1177-1071181322661236. This matters because doi-10-1016-j-eswa-2021-115626 contributes to the HIGH-confidence finding about temporal preference modeling.

The theme stating that "Novelty and non-repetition depend on previously selected or summarized context rather than text similarity alone" is stronger than the supplied analyses establish. MMR explicitly uses similarity to already selected material, Summary Cloze shows benefits from preceding-summary context and uses coverage to discourage repetition, and TREC evaluates novelty, but these studies do not establish a general necessity claim that novelty/non-repetition depends on such context or that text-similarity-only methods are categorically insufficient.

The actionable recommendation to include both a triggering work item and intended action in reminder-like briefing entries is grounded principally in doi-10-3758-bf03201140, a simplified laboratory prospective-memory setting. The workplace reminder paper 2403.01365 supports forgotten-task value and state-sensitive reminder interaction, but does not experimentally establish the target-plus-action reminder format. The recommendation should be labeled as a transfer-derived design hypothesis rather than a directly validated workplace rule.

The actionable recommendation to expose uncertainty as structured workplace state is a reasonable synthesis direction, but direct evidence is adjacent-domain evidence from uncertainty communication and misinformation studies. Gap-7 correctly says workplace presentation remains unevaluated, so the recommendation should preserve that qualification to avoid sounding like an empirically validated workplace intervention.

Finding 8 says that previously presented context "can reduce repetition." Summary Cloze demonstrates that preceding-summary context improves content selection/generation and that its architecture is designed to discourage repetition, but the supplied analysis does not report a direct repetition-reduction outcome. MMR provides some redundancy-reduction evidence, though its multi-document result is explicitly preliminary. The wording should distinguish demonstrated contextual benefit from directly measured repetition reduction.
unsupported_claims: "Two admitted sources are abstract-only" is factually inconsistent with the supplied analyses; there are three abstract-only sources.
"Novelty and non-repetition depend on previously selected or summarized context rather than text similarity alone" overstates the evidence as a general dependency/necessity claim.

Any interpretation of the target-plus-action reminder recommendation as an empirically validated workplace design rule would be unsupported; the direct experimental evidence is from laboratory prospective-memory tasks.

Any interpretation of structured uncertainty presentation as already validated for longitudinal workplace briefings would be unsupported; the synthesis itself correctly identifies this as an open gap.
required_fixes: Correct the abstract-only limitation to include doi-10-1016-j-eswa-2021-115626 and state that three admitted sources are abstract-only.

Revise the novelty/non-repetition theme to a weaker claim, for example that prior selected or summarized context is useful for novelty control and repetition avoidance in the evaluated settings, without claiming it is necessary or superior to text similarity in general.
Qualify the target-plus-action reminder recommendation as transfer-derived from laboratory prospective-memory evidence and not yet validated in workplace briefings.
Qualify the structured-uncertainty recommendation as a design hypothesis supported by adjacent uncertainty literature, consistent with gap-7 remaining open.

Revise Finding 8 so that Summary Cloze is credited with improved context-conditioned content selection/generation and an anti-repetition design mechanism, while direct redundancy-reduction evidence is attributed cautiously to MMR because its multi-document evidence is preliminary.
notes: The synthesis is substantially faithful and appropriately conservative about the absence of an integrated longitudinal workplace briefing system. All cited paper_ids are from the permitted set, transfer-domain evidence is generally identified as such, all eight central gaps remain explicitly open, and no gap is falsely presented as closed. The empty contradictions list is defensible because the supplied analyses do not expose a clear cross-paper contradiction under comparable questions and conditions; the most visible reversals or trade-offs arise from different datasets, objectives, or experimental conditions. The identified problems are correctable wording and evidence-strength issues rather than failures of the central synthesis.
